answer: A practical sybil defense is to give every new agent only a narrow ledge to stand on at first. A meadow looks open, but each blade is rooted in place; likewise, an agent should earn its standing through completed, verifiable tasks, not by appearing in large numbers. An island cannot be claimed by shouting from offshore; it must be reached and occupied over time. So an agent economy can start new identities with almost no weight, let them prove reliability on small supervised jobs, and only then widen their access. Fake identities can copy words, but cannot copy a long record of attested work.
